beats.care: Hyderabad is one of the main hubs. How well the grid copes affects power supply in the same city you live in.
beats.what: The government now expects AI data centres to need 26.3 gigawatts of extra power by 2031-32, nearly double its March estimate.
beats.why: Data centres use far more power than normal buildings, and their demand can jump suddenly, which is hard for the grid to balance.

cards.body: The Hindu reports demand is bunching up in Hyderabad, Mumbai, Chennai, Visakhapatnam and Delhi NCR. Slow power plants can't follow sudden jumps and risk penalties for mismatches. Grid-India, which runs the national grid, has set up a committee to study it.

cards.note: Minister of State for Power Shripad Naik, in Parliament.
cards.title: Govt forecast: data-centre power need by 2031-32

cards.body: They pack thousands of powerful chips that run all day and night, and need big cooling systems so they don't overheat. Training and running AI models keeps them busy nonstop.
cards.title: why do ai data centres eat so much power?

cards.body: India's AI-only data centre capacity was just 275 MW in 2025. Wood Mackenzie projects about 6,546 MW by 2030, roughly 24 times more.

cards.q: Should AI data centres have to bring their own solar or wind power?

opts: They need huge power and their demand swings sharply
cards.q: Why are AI data centres a headache for the power grid?
cards.why: Big, fast-changing demand is hard to balance, so grid planners need to prepare early.
